First incursion across boundary since ceasefire deal comes as Eisenkot seeks to form government without Netanyahu
The Israeli military crossed into Hamas-controlled central Gaza on Wednesday in its first ground operation across the “yellow line” boundary since a fragile ceasefire was agreed last October, forcing dozens of displaced Palestinians to flee their tents.
Israeli tanks rolled along the Salah al-Din road , Gaza’s main north-south route, a day after the US-backed Board of Peace, a body overseeing the ceasefire, accused Israel and Hamas of failing to honour their commitments to end hostilities.
An Israeli military spokesperson said troops were carrying out an operation targeting “Hamas infrastructure” west of the yellow line in central Gaza .
The operation lasted about 24 hours and on Thursday the military said it had been “completed”.
The IDF ​has not commented extensively on the operation, which came as the Israeli opposition politician, Gadi Eisenkot, has been seeking to form a government without the caretaker prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, who has built his political reputation on promises to keep Israel safe.
A Gaza security source told AFP there was “intense Israeli artillery shelling” north of Nuseirat refugee camp and reported Israeli military vehicles in central Gaza “amid ongoing gunfire and airstrikes since midday”.
Hamas condemned the Israeli raid and the forced displacement of Palestinians as “a flagrant violation of the ceasefire agreement” and a dangerous escalation. The Israeli military did not immediately respond to Hamas’s statement.
Residents reported hearing tank fire in the area. Palestinian medics said one person was killed in an Israeli airstrike near the site of the raid.
After the statement from the IDF that it had concluded the tank raid to dismantle a suspected Hamas tunnel, the defence ministry’s body in charge of civilian affairs in Palestinian territories, Cogat, said Palestinians would again be free to move in the targeted areas near al-Bureij and Nuseirat refugee camps.
In separate incidents on Wednesday, Palestinian medics said two people were killed by Israeli fire, one in Deir al-Balah and the other in Gaza City. The Israeli military said it was unaware of any incident in Deir al-Balah and had struck a militant in Gaza City.
Israel has stepped up its attacks on Hamas, which it says has been regrouping and rearming. Hamas has accused Israel of trying to derail the US-brokered ceasefire agreed in October 2025.
Israeli strikes have continued since the ceasefire, and Hamas remains armed.
Last week, an Israeli airstrike on Nasser hospital in southern Gaza killed six people, including a surgeon and a disabled man, and wounded 28 others, according to the hospital director.
The body overseeing Donald Trump’s plan to end the war in Gaza has accused Israel and Hamas of failing to honour their commitments to end hostilities, leaving Palestinians in dire conditions and the ceasefire at risk of collapse.
In its second report to the UN security council since the truce began 13 months ago, the Trump-led Board of Peace said the gap between what was agreed and what was happening on the ground remained the biggest threat to the deal. The report, seen by Reuters, warned that “a ceasefire that delivers nothing visible cannot be sustained indefinitely”.
Gaza’s health authorities say at least 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the ceasefire came into effect. The Israeli military says five of its soldiers have been killed over the same period.
Palestinian authorities say more than 74,000 people have been killed in Gaza since Israel launched its military campaign in response to the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, in which about 1,200 people were killed.
In June, an ⁠independent UN inquiry determined that Israel was continuing to commit genocide by deliberately targeting Palestinian children. A previous report by the commission in September 2025 found that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza , and Israeli officials, including the prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, incited those acts. Netanyahu is separately wanted by the international criminal court (ICC) for war crimes.

Residents fled the area near Nuseirat and Bureij refugee camps following the Israeli evacuation order
Israeli forces have completed a rare ground operation in part of central Gaza outside their control, the military says, a day after residents were ordered to evacuate.
Families fled their homes and tents on Wednesday as tanks advanced into an area east of Nuseirat refugee camp and onto the territory's main north-south road under the cover of artillery strikes.
The Israeli military said the "targeted" operation aimed to dismantle a "terror tunnel" west of the so-called Yellow Line, which marks the more than 60% of Gaza's territory occupied by Israel.
The Palestinian armed group Hamas, which controls the rest of Gaza, accused Israel of a "flagrant violation" of the October 2025 ceasefire deal.
Violence has continued in Gaza over the past 13 months, with near-daily Israeli strikes, and living conditions for the 2.1 million people there remain dire.
Wednesday's Israeli incursion deep beyond the Yellow Line was reportedly the first to be publicly announced by the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) since the ceasefire began.
In the early afternoon, Israeli military body Cogat's Arabic spokesperson announced the start of the operation and warned Palestinians living in an area north of Nuseirat and Bureij refugee camp to stay away for their own safety. It also said a section of Salah al-Din road that passed through the area would be closed to traffic.
In the evening, the IDF said the joint operation with the Shin Bet security service sought "to dismantle a terror tunnel west of the Yellow Line that posed an immediate and direct threat to IDF troops".
On Thursday morning, Cogat told Palestinians on social media that "the activity has ended, and the Salah al-Din axis has been reopened".
Hamas warned in a statement that the advance of Israeli military vehicles beyond the Yellow Line and the evacuation of residents constituted "a dangerous development and a flagrant violation of the ceasefire agreement".
Gaza's Hamas-run government media office meanwhile said that an estimated 6,000 people had fled their homes and tents because of the operation, and that this amounted to the war crime of forced displacement.
Footage published by Palestinian media outlets and on social media showed dozens of families fleeing areas near Nuseirat camp following the Israeli evacuation order.
In one video verified by BBC Verify, a man could be seen ducking after hearing artillery fire and then running along Salah al-Din road, about 1.5km (0.9 miles) west of the Yellow Line. "The Israeli occupation now is firing randomly near the houses and tents of people," he said.
An image, meanwhile, showed six armoured vehicles, including tanks and bulldozers, around Salah al-Din road.
A resident of Nuseirat who was forced to flee told BBC Arabic's Middle East Daily programme: "The situation is now extremely dire, with Israeli forces firing indiscriminately at areas where displaced people have sought shelter."
"We couldn't take any of our belongings with us - not even our blankets, pillows, or clothes. We had no choice but to leave everything behind."
A second resident also reported "indiscriminate gunfire and shelling" and said there had been "numerous casualties, including fatalities".
Asked about those reports, the IDF sent a general statement about the operation.
Multiple verified videos of the aftermath of the incursion on Thursday showed destruction, earth banks, and heavy vehicle tracks more than 1.2km beyond the Yellow Line.
That is believed to be the furthest Israeli troops have advanced into central Gaza since they occupied the so-called Netzarim Corridor before the ceasefire.
Some residents returned to check their properties following the Israeli withdrawal.
"The entire area has been destroyed, and we honestly do not know what to do," Abd Aliwa told Reuters news agency as he sat beside a pile of rubble.

Israel moves Yellow Line deeper into Gaza, satellite images show
Gaza's Hamas-run Civil Defence agency said three people were killed and others were wounded in three separate Israeli drone strikes on Wednesday.
One man was killed in Nuseirat, the second was killed to the north in Gaza City, and the third was killed in the central town of Deir al-Balah, it added.
The IDF told the BBC that it had "struck several military operatives".
Gaza health officials said another two people were killed on Thursday by Israeli fire in eastern Gaza City, according to Reuters. There was no immediate comment from the IDF.
At least 1,662 people have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza since the ceasefire began last year, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.
The Israeli military says six of its soldiers have been killed over the same period.
Meanwhile, more than 1.9 million people - about 90% of Gaza's population - remain displaced, with 1.4 million of them living in tents or makeshift shelters, according to the UN.
Reconstruction has yet to begin in Gaza, where an estimated 82% of all structures have been destroyed or damaged during the war, as US President Donald Trump's peace plan has largely stalled.
The group has agreed to give up its weapons in exchange for a phased withdrawal of Israeli troops from the 60% of Gaza they currently occupy. But Israel has insisted that Hamas must fully disarm before any pullout.
The war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage.
Since then, more than 74,710 people have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza, its health ministry says.

The presidents of China, the US and Russia have held an unprecedented summit. While Trump said the three leaders were "making history," Xi described the talks as "fruitful" and Putin called them "open and candid."
Chinese President Xi Jinping hosted US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday for an unprecedented trilateral summit in Shenzhen, bringing together the leaders of the world's three most powerful military powers amid heightened geopolitical tensions.
Xi hailed the talks as "groundbreaking," saying discussions ranged from global governance and denuclearization to the war in Ukraine and energy security.
The "peace declaration" released after their meeting made no mention of Russia's war in Ukraine or the US-led war in Iran.
Instead, the three leaders agreed to pursue reforms of the United Nations, limit the role of the International Criminal Court and reaffirm their commitment to avoiding nuclear war. They also pledged to boost supplies of refined petroleum products to address global energy challenges.
The tightly choreographed meeting fueled concerns that Beijing, Washington and Moscow could seek to reshape the international order around competing spheres of influence.
While Xi said the talks with Trump and Putin were "positive, constructive and fruitful," Trump heralded the gathering as "really making history."
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
For Putin, the three-way talks, and his meetings with both leaders separately earlier, offered a chance to show the world that he was on par with the leaders of the US and China, despite Western efforts to isolate him since he launched the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
Emma Chanlett-Avery, senior director for Political-Security Affairs at the Asia Society Policy Institute (ASPI), said Putin had the most to gain from the meeting as "he appeared on the world stage as one of the dominant players in the world."
Chim Lee, a senior analyst with The Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU), echoed this view.
The meeting itself is a "major outcome for Russia," he told DW, pointing to Russian media coverage that has cast it as "reinforcing Russia's standing in the world."
The joint statement also said the leaders are committed to work to reduce nuclear risks and prevent nuclear proliferation.
The last nuclear arms pact between Russia and the United States, known as New START, expired in February.
Trump has said he wants "a new, improved and modernized" deal that includes China.
But Beijing has so far been reluctant to accept limits as its estimated arsenal of around 500 warheads remains far smaller than those of Russia and the US.
Moscow and Washington are believed to possess more than 5,000 warheads each.
Lee said China is unlikely to participate in a trilateral institutionalized setting to control nuclear arms.
"The gap between China's nuclear arsenal and those of Russia and US is still quite large. From China's perspective, it doesn't seem to make a lot of sense to put the three powers in the same bucket in this area."
The expert believes Trump attended the meeting as he is "actively thinking about his legacy in the final two years in office."
"So, in this context, the idea of setting up a trilateral nuclear arms control arrangement would have been a very big achievement," Lee said.
But, in the end, the declaration said the countries would merely engage in "dialogue" on the issue, avoiding any explicit commitments to downsize their nuclear stockpiles.
China initially hesitated to organize the trilateral summit as it did not want to be explicitly tied to Russia's war in Ukraine and harm Beijing's efforts to present itself as a long-term force for global stability.
The Chinese government, which is working to rebalance economic ties with the EU, was also wary of appearing to form a G3 club with Washington and Moscow, which could alienate other global partners.
Chanlett-Avery said that China had some degree of discomfort in convening this meeting, worried about getting involved in Ukraine issues.
But Beijing eventually "managed to get the outcome they wanted" and kept the European conflict out of the meeting's focus, she noted.
"China was able to show off Shenzhen and all of its sparkling high-tech features. They convened a successful international meeting that grabbed lots of headlines," she added. "So, I think China probably came out feeling okay."
Prior to the summit, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had warned of a "second Yalta," referring to the Yalta Conference held in Crimea in 1945.
That meeting saw the Allied powers decide on the post-war European order following the end of World War II.
In Shenzhen, Putin stressed that Russia, the US and China, as victors in World War II and veto-wielding members of the UN Security Council, bore a "joint responsibility for maintaining international peace."
But Ying-Yu Lin, Associate Professor at Graduate Institute of International Affairs and Strategic Studies at Taiwan's Tamkang University, said the Yalta comparison "is a bit of a stretch," given the vast differences between 1945 and now.
Putin also said that all three leaders "agree that it's a useful format," and such meetings could take place again.
Lee, the EIU expert, said the trilateral setup "is unlikely to be just a one-off" and there will probably be more such meetings in the coming years.
"Especially from the US side to have this kind of setup, there will be some interest in maintaining warm relations with both China and Russia," he underlined.

US President Donald Trump has “sharply questioned” European countries over their continued financial support for Ukraine during the country’s conflict with Russia.
The president unexpectedly phoned into a meeting of Ukraine’s European allies on Thursday, according to the Politico publication, which heard from four European officials who were briefed on the discussion.
He asked the allies why they were continuing to spend billions on military support for Kyiv.
The call came mere hours after Trump wrapped up a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and his Chinese counterpart, President Xi Jinping, in Shenzhen, China.
The US president is said to have called Berlin from his private aircraft, Air Force One, and insisted that Putin was serious about future peace negotiations about Ukraine.
Three of the European officials, who have been granted anonymity, said that Trump was strongly sceptical about the possibility of further aid being provided to Ukraine by the Coalition of the Willing, an alliance of 34 countries – plus Ukraine – who have pledged strengthened support for Ukraine against Russian aggression.
One of the officials said Trump bemoaned the fact that a lot of people are dying in the conflict, and a lot of money is being “wasted” on the nearly five-year-long war. That official also confirmed that the US leader believes Putin will cooperate with peace negotiations with Ukraine.

European leaders have said they are ready for negotiations with Russia on ending the war in Ukraine, in a strong show of support for Kyiv.
"Europe has a clear and consistent and united negotiating position," UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said, while German Chancellor Friedrich Merz stressed that Moscow's "maximalist demands are not realistic".
They were speaking at Berlin's summit of Ukraine's allies known as the Coalition of the Willing.
Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner, one of the two US envoys who were in Berlin, said the US president wanted to make a deal with Moscow "with Europe by his side". Russia's Vladimir Putin has so far rejected any European role in the US-led peace talks.
Trump had earlier held historic trilateral talks in Shenzhen , south-eastern China, with Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping and later dialled into the Berlin summit from Air Force One.
In a lengthy press conference following his talks with Trump and Xi, Putin addressed the question of multilateral peace talks, saying the Americans were "insistently" asking Russia to allow the Europeans to take part.
Putin claimed Russia was not against the idea but said Moscow wanted to clarify "what Europe will bring to these talks".
"That is why, through diplomatic channels, we have invited the Europeans to come to Moscow in order to determine their positions. And after that, we will decide in what format we will continue the dialogue with Ukraine."
But Putin also said that "every day" Russia heard that European leaders were talking about war coming in 2030. "But we are not planning to attack anyone... Is that normal? I do not think so," he said. Still, Putin added, Russia understood that "discussing issues linked to security in Europe is pointless without the Europeans".
Jared Kushner told reporters that the US president had come away from Shenzhen believing that "peace is achievable".
Striking an upbeat note, Kushner said that the Russians were willing to trust the instinct of the US envoys "on our behalf" that the Europeans should be at the table and that Moscow was now "comfortable" with Ukraine having security guarantees based on the idea enshrined in Nato's Article Five that requires allies to come to a country's defence if it comes under attack.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, who also was at the summit in Germany's capital, has long sought a guarantee equivalent to Nato's collective defence clause, and there has been little indication that Putin would accept that kind of condition.
Russia rejects outright the idea of Ukrainian membership of Nato, but reports say US negotiators have mulled the idea of giving Kyiv Article Five-style guarantees without being part of the Western defensive alliance if it agrees to painful territorial concessions.
Zelensky and the three European leaders – Merz, Burnham and French President Emmanuel Macron – were not as upbeat as Kushner, and the Ukrainian president made clear that the Russian president had spurned every proposal so far: "Putin has always said no."
The German chancellor was equally sceptical, although he said with US involvement the chance of peace was increasing. Europe was willing to enter "serious discussions on European security" with Russia, he explained, "as long as it's matched with a serious discussion and only first a peace agreement with Ukraine".
"These talks have to begin, and we will accept if conditions are acceptable for Europe and Ukraine," said Merz.
He also said any attempts to divide Europe into spheres of influence run by major powers was unacceptable, amid concerns on the continent that this issue may have been on the agenda at the trilateral talks in Shenzhen.
Analysis: Trilateral summit high on spectacle, short on substance
"A 'Yalta format' will not bring peace," Merz said, referring to the post-World War Two agreement between the US, the USSR and Britain in 1945.
He also sought to downplay the Shenzhen summit as above all "a photo opportunity."
"The US understands that there can be no peace without us. We, in turn, know that with the United States by our side, the prospects for peace increase," Merz added.
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk also took exception to Trump's description of Putin as a "friend" at the Shenzhen summit, saying: "Mr Putin is not our friend and will never be."
Meanwhile, Macron urged Ukraine's allies to do the "maximum" to deliver the much-needed air defence systems Kyiv needed to repel deadly Russian attacks.
The French leader also urged the allies to "reopen the question" of Ukraine's membership in Nato.
There have been mixed messages from Moscow on European participation to the talks. Last week, following a visit to Moscow, the US envoys, Steve Witkoff and Kushner, appeared certain that Europe would soon have a seat at the negotiating table.
But the Russians were more circumspect and this week Putin's aide Yury Ushakov said a "great deal" would have to be done before the format could be expanded, suggesting that several more rounds of discussions would have to be held before any four-sided talks could take place.
Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
Several buildings were damaged in the latest Russian attack on Ukraine's capital Kyiv
While Russia has engaged with several rounds of talks over the last year, little in Moscow's rhetoric or actions suggests that the Kremlin is considering scaling down its war on Ukraine.
It continues to pound Kyiv's energy infrastructure to cripple it as winter takes hold, increasing numbers of civilian casualties are being recorded across the country, and Kremlin officials have not budged from Russia's demands for Ukrainian sovereign territory.
As delegations were meeting in China and Germany on Thursday, several buildings in Kyiv's historic centre came under attack from drones. One person was killed in a strike on a residential building in the Podilskyi neighbourhood, while the Dutch and Austrian embassies as well as Saint Volodymyr's Cathedral reported damage.
And Putin also vowed that Moscow's response to a Ukrainian strike on the Crimean Bridge linking Russia with occupied Crimea would be "considerably more painful" than what Kyiv had achieved.
He also said he had discussed a "possible ceasefire in a number of areas" but had decided against it after the attack on the bridge.
Still, Putin claimed to be "interested" in ending the war and was ready to make compromises, while Ukraine and Europe were not.
"I assure you, we have no desire at all to continue this armed conflict," Putin said, despite the fact that Russia has in recent months intensified its attacks on Ukraine's critical infrastructure as cold winter approaches.
Kyiv and its European allies say that – in the absence of any major success on the vast front line – the Kremlin leader is seeking to break Ukrainian resistance by leaving millions of civilians without electricity and water supply.

Police say the raid targeted the Martissant area, located on a key route out of Port-au-Prince held by gangs since 2021.
At least 34 suspected gang members were killed in a police operation in Martissant, a neighbourhood in Haiti’s capital that has been under gang control for more than five years, Haitian police said.
Haiti’s National Police, which posted footage of armoured vehicles moving through the neighbourhood, said their officers carried out the raid on Thursday with an anti-gang task force that includes personnel from Vectus Global, the private security firm founded by Blackwater founder Erik Prince.
Police reported no other casualties and said none of the roughly 2,500 Salvadoran troops in Haiti took part.
The Martissant neighbourhood is located along a key road that connects Port-au-Prince to Haiti’s western and southern cities, and was used by thousands of people daily before rival gangs began fighting to control the area in 2021.
The subsequent violence forced at least 19,000 people to flee their homes, according to a July 2022 UN report.
Armed groups have since demanded payment for using the road or shot at cars that have tried to pass through, making it difficult to bring goods in and out of the city.
Separately, the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force said it was stepping up operations in Tabarre after months of night patrols and efforts to identify gang positions.
“The objective is clear: not just to displace gangs, but to dismantle their hold on communities, reclaim territory, and prevent their return,” the force said on X.
In the central Artibonite region, the force said their troops had come under fire while clearing barricades and filling in trenches that gangs had dug along National Route 5, north of the town of Gros-Morne.
“During the operation, gang members opened fire on GSF personnel, who responded and forced them to withdraw,” said the update on X.
The raid in Martissant comes as Salvadoran troops have been carrying out joint operations with Haitian police. El Salvador’s President Nayib Bukele initially sent troops to search for four Salvadoran aviation technicians who went missing after an October 18 ambush near Port-au-Prince.
What began as a search for the missing men has since grown into a broader offensive against Haiti’s gangs.

Judge in Florida says an expert has determined the 82-year-old estranged father of the Duchess of Sussex is mentally competent to face charges
An expert has determined that Thomas Markle, the 82-year-old estranged father of the Duchess of Sussex , is mentally competent to face charges of keeping child sexual abuse material in storage in California, a judge said on Thursday.
Markle’s defense lawyer said they would not contest the finding by Dr Amie Gerodimos. The exam was ordered after his arrest at a senior care center in Lakeland, Florida , on 6 November.
Investigators seized approximately 78 items from two storage units rented by Markle in the Los Angeles area, including slides, film negatives and books that contained suspected child sexual abuse images, according to the FBI .
Some images appear to depict him with children, the FBI said.
Markle is in custody while the case remains in federal court in Tampa. It will eventually shift to a similar court in southern California .
Markle was initially released on bond but was arrested again when authorities accused him of cutting off his electronic ankle monitor on 10 November.
He had a stroke earlier this year while living in the Philippines and had to have his left leg amputated. That forced him to return to the US and settle in Florida.
The Sun, a British tabloid newspaper, reported that Meghan’s half-brother found child sexual abuse images while clearing out their father’s home in the Philippines. The discovery led to a search of the two US storage units in California, which Markle had rented since 2008.
Meanwhile, in the Philippines, Markle is under investigation for possession and intent to distribute images. The Women and Children Protection Center, a branch of the Philippine national police, filed a formal criminal complaint against Markle on Monday, police spokesperson Brig Gen Allen Rae Co said in a written statement.
The complaint was filed with the prosecutor’s office following an investigation into digital devices found at Markle’s former home in Cebu City, the statement said. The prosecutor’s office will assess the case for possible charges.
Markle did not attend his daughter Meghan’s 2018 wedding to Prince Harry at Windsor Castle. She said at the time he needed to tend to his health. Meghan is an American citizen who starred in the US television drama Suits.

Yönetmeliğe göre, Kanun kapsamında belediye başkanlığının veya belediye başkanvekilliğinin herhangi bir nedenle boşalması halinde belediye başkanlığı veya belediye başkanvekilliği seçimi vali tarafından 10 gün içinde kararlaştırılacak.

Six people, including a child, have been killed after a suspected natural gas explosion caused part of a five-storey apartment building to collapse in Georgia’s capital, Tbilisi, according to the AFP news agency.
The blast struck the residential building in the suburban Ponichala district on Thursday morning, trapping several residents beneath the rubble.
Georgian Interior Minister Sulkhan Tamazashvili said rescuers had recovered six bodies from the wreckage, including that of a young child.
A three-year-old girl was pulled alive from the rubble after several hours of rescue operations, prompting applause from onlookers gathered at the scene.
Emergency Management Service chief Teimuraz Mgebrishvili said one of the women found dead was believed to be the girl’s mother, according to AFP.
Doctors at Ingorokva University Clinic said the rescued girl was in stable condition and scans had revealed no serious traumatic injuries, Georgian Public Broadcaster (1TV) reported.
An 11-year-old boy was also being treated in intensive care, although his condition was described as relatively stable, according to the broadcaster.
Tamazashvili said preliminary findings indicated that the explosion occurred on the fifth floor when a resident attempted to switch on a gas heater.
However, gas supplier Tbilisi Energy said the apartment identified as the likely source of the explosion had been registered as unoccupied and had recorded no gas consumption over the past year, according to 1TV. The company said it had not yet been able to inspect the damaged property.
Tbilisi Mayor Kakha Kaladze said authorities would temporarily relocate 28 families, comprising more than 100 residents, to hotels after structural assessments found two sections of the building unsafe, according to Georgia’s Interpressnews agency.
Prosecutor Levan Vepkhvadze said a criminal investigation had been launched into possible violations of safety regulations.

A judge in Florida has declared Thomas Markle Sr, the father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, to be mentally competent to stand trial for possessing indecent images of children.
The hearing came after an evaluation by a court-appointed psychiatrist conducted on Prince Harry's 82-year-old father-in-law.
Markle, who has denied possessing images of child sex abuse, was ordered to stay in jail pending trial earlier this month after allegedly removing a location monitoring device.
The FBI arrested Markle on 6 November at an elderly care home that specialises in dementia. His arrest came after a search of a storage unit he had allegedly rented in Los Angeles uncovered the abuse material.
Markle appeared in court in Tampa in a wheelchair, and his lawyers did not dispute the court-appointed psychiatrist's finding that he is mentally competent to understand the nature and consequences of the charge against him.
His next court hearing is scheduled for early December, but any trial is expected to take place in California, where the federal charge was filed.
Inside the storage units in Los Angeles the FBI says agents found about 78 items, including film negatives, slides and books that they allege contained child sex abuse material.
Witnesses "positively identified" Markle in two of the images believed to contain child sex abuse material.
In those images, the man pictured "appears to be in the age range of 30s to 40s", which suggests the alleged abuse dates back decades.
He moved to the Philippines last year after he had a series of strokes, and lived in Cebu until May. He was reportedly learning to walk again in Florida after having his leg amputated.
On Monday, police in the Philippines asked prosecutors to charge Markle with possession of and intent to distribute child sexual abuse material.
Last month, police there obtained a warrant to examine devices allegedly removed from Markle's former home in the country.
Four boxes of material, including computers, phones, hard drives and old video tapes, were handed to officers by Meghan's half brother Thomas Markle Jr.
The duchess has been estranged from her father since 2018, and he did not attend her wedding in London that same year.
The BBC understands she broke contact with him last year, telling him she and the authorities knew he had abused young girls.
In a previously shared statement, Meghan confirmed the existence of the letter and wrote: "I am deeply distressed... my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed."
She said she hoped it could be understood why she had largely cut off contact from her father and did "not allow him to have contact with our children".

Rohingya refugees watch the International Court of Justice ruling over whether Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya Muslims, on a screen at a camp in Bangladesh's Cox's Bazar on Nov. 19. Salahuddin Ahmed/AFP via Getty Images hide caption
The United Nations' top court ruled Thursday that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority, the first time in the court's 80-year history that it has held a state responsible for the crime.
Judges of the International Court of Justice voted 9-6 that the military's 2017 crackdown was carried out with intent to destroy the long-persecuted Muslim minority. Myanmar's military-backed government has not yet responded to the ruling at the time of writing.
Brought by Gambia under the 1948 Genocide Convention, the ruling will have repercussions far beyond Myanmar, according to a legal expert.
But for Ma Roga Bibi, a Rohingya who fled Maungdaw township in northern Rakhine state, the impact was immediate.
"I feel wonderful and grateful," said the 18-year-old, who lives in the world's largest refugee settlement in Bangladesh. "It was an emotional, historic day."
For several weeks in August and September 2017, the Myanmar military attacked and burned to the ground hundreds of Rohingya villages. Soldiers committed rapes and massacred women, men as well as children.
The court estimated that about 10,000 Rohingya were killed. It cited estimates that up to 2,109 Rohingya children younger than 5 died, and found the violence was systematic, including the burning of all or parts of 392 villages.
Judges of the International Court of Justice (ICJ) attend a public hearing ahead of the reading of the court's judgment in the genocide case brought by Gambia against Myanmar, in The Hague on Thursday. Jeroen Jumelet/ANP/AFP via Getty Images hide caption
Ma Roga Bibi, then age 9, was one of about 700,000 people to flee to Bangladesh, joining earlier refugee waves. The camps sprawl across a narrow coastal strip a few miles from Cox's Bazar, a busy beach town near Myanmar. Rohingya are denied citizenship on both sides of the border.
"Recognition alone is not enough," she said. "We need justice, accountability, and the opportunity to return home with dignity."
She wants to be a doctor, adding, "in our Rohingya community, there is no girl doctor."
Khin Khin Myint, 18, a refugee leader in activist group Rohingya Youth Voice from Buthidaung Township, also in Camp 16, said Rohingya women and girls have experienced "unimaginable suffering."
"We want the world to listen to survivors, recognize their courage, and include women in decisions about our future," she said. "We expect the international community to move beyond a statement of sympathy."
Myanmar had argued its military was conducting counterinsurgency operations against an armed group, the Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army. The court said the military failed to distinguish between civilians and alleged insurgents, and that the scale and nature of the violence could not be explained by counterterrorism.
"The execution of Rohingya men and boys in some locations, the widespread sexual violence, the targeting of children and babies, the methodical burning of villages, and attacks on fleeing civilians are not consistent with an intent to conduct counterinsurgency operations," said ICJ president, Judge Yuji Iwasawa.
Rohingya refugees watch the International Court of Justice ruling over whether Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya Muslims, on a screen at a camp in Bangladesh's Cox's Bazar, on Thursday. Salahuddin Ahmed/AFP via Getty Images hide caption
Antonia Mulvey, executive director of Legal Action Worldwide, a human rights group based in Geneva, said the court found evidence from the U.N. and rights organizations credible, and that counterterrorism operations were not a defense to Myanmar's argument.
She said the ruling will affect future genocide cases, including South Africa's case against Israel , on questions such as genocidal intent and state responsibility.
"Although every case must ultimately be decided on its own evidence," she said.
The judgment is binding on Myanmar and on all states that have ratified the Genocide Convention, she explained. All countries should review trade agreements, including arms and jet fuel supplies, and financial and economic ties with the junta, she said, while supporting accountability and reparations for the Rohingya. But the court, which hears disputes between states, can't enforce its decisions.
In Myanmar, Rohingya are widely regarded as interlopers from Bangladesh, despite generations of roots in Myanmar.
Iwasawa, however, identified the Rohingya as a distinct ethnic group, saying their language and art set them apart, and that they self-identify as such. He said they have been discriminated against by Myanmar "for decades" and qualify as a protected group.
The United States had previously reached a similar conclusion. In 2022, the Biden administration formally determined that Myanmar's military had committed genocide and crimes against humanity against the Rohingya during its 2016 and 2017 operations.
But tensions have mounted between the Trump administration and international justice bodies. In a statement to NPR on Thursday, the State Department expressed support for Rohingya refugees but raised doubts about the International Court of Justice. "The proper interpretation of the Genocide Convention is of paramount importance, as is preventing politicization of the ICJ. We are studying the decision to fully assess its implications," the State Department said.
In October, U.S. Ambassador to the U.N. Mike Waltz wrote online , "The ICJ must not be allowed to lower the legal threshold for proving genocide" so it can later be weaponized against U.S. and allied soldiers.
Yet international human rights organizations and the United Nations applauded the court's judgment.
U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres called it "a powerful recognition of the Rohingya victims of genocide" and said it reaffirms that "impunity for such horrific acts must not stand."
The judgment does not order Myanmar to grant citizenship, saying such the issue fell outside the scope of the measures being considered to prevent future atrocities.
However, Myanmar must take steps to investigate people suspected of involvement in the crimes and prosecute them if warranted, said the court. It also found Myanmar must provide restitution and compensation, with the amount to be set in future proceedings.
The order to enable displaced Rohingya to return runs into a hard reality: The territory is now controlled by ethnic Rakhine armed group the Arakan Army.
Rakhine state has been ravaged by conflict between the military and the group, which now controls most of it.
Su Mon, a senior analyst at the independent conflict monitor Armed Conflict Location & Event Data, said the Rohingya in Myanmar and in the camps are "threatened by multiple armed groups," including Rohingya armed groups, the Arakan Army and the military.
Nearly all are stateless, she said, with few viable ways to earn a living or get food. Many are "on the verge of acute famine" because of aid shortfalls in the camps and a junta blockade in Rakhine.
"Unless the broader conflict dynamics in Rakhine state improve or credible guarantees of safety are secured from all armed actors, the prospects for displaced Rohingya to return to their homes remain bleak," she added.
She urged the military to halt airstrikes, drone attacks and the use of advanced weaponry in northern Rakhine, lift its blockade and give humanitarian groups full access, including in Arakan Army-controlled areas.
Lorcán Lovett reported from Thailand. Michele Kelemen contributed reporting from Washington, D.C.

Osian Morgan has previously appeared in Pobol y Cwm and Waterloo Road
Voicing Luke Skywalker in the Welsh-language version of Star Wars was a "dream job" according to actor Osian Morgan.
The Cardiff-born actor said he loved the film series as a child and playing one of the lead roles was "very exciting".
Star Wars: Gobaith Newydd - based on the original 1977 film Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope - was given its first showing at a red-carpet event in Cardiff on Thursday.
The dubbed Welsh version, featuring actors Matthew Rhys and Rhys Ifans, will be broadcast publicly for the first time by S4C on Christmas Day.
Star Wars: Gobaith Newydd (S4C, STAR WARS a Cymru Creadigol)
Almost half a century since A New Hope was first released, the sci-fi universe created by George Lucas remains one of the biggest film franchises of all time.
It has been translated into over 50 languages, with Welsh becoming its most recent.
"It feels very exciting, it's thrilling," said Morgan, who has previously starred in Welsh language soap opera Pobol y Cwm and in BBC drama Waterloo Road.
His family attended the first screening of Star Wars: Gobaith Newydd, and Morgan admitted his youngest brother had never seen any of the films before.
"Shout out to him because the first time he gets to see it in Welsh is great," he said.
The film's premiere in Cardiff included a rousing version of the theme tune
Mark Lewis Jones, who voices the dark lord Darth Vader, said on the red carpet it was "nice to record the voice but not have the make-up" and joked that "the Rhosllanerchrugog accent lends itself to the dark side".
Llyr Ifans, who plays C-3PO, said he hoped the film was successful and that more Welsh-language versions would follow.
"I'm quite confident it will go down well and there will be a lot of happy Welsh-speaking parents on Christmas Day."
Ifans said he been a fan of the Star Wars films since childhood, and getting invited to play the character was "surreal".
"When I first got the email through I thought 'wow, this is a bit weird doing Star Wars in Welsh' but playing C-3PO, one of the iconic parts, you can't say no, can you really?"
C-3PO is said to be fluent in six million forms of communication and Ifans said it was now one more.
Mark Lewis Jones, who voices Darth Vader, joked his accent 'lent itself to the dark side'
Prominent actors have lent their voices to the film's most famous characters, including Matthew Rhys (Han Solo), Rhys Ifans (Obi-Wan Kenobi) and Aimee-Ffion Edwards (Princess Leia).
Other voice actors in the Welsh version include Nia Roberts, Ioan Hefin, Richard Harrington, Owain Arthur, Rhodri Meilir, Richard Elfyn and Steffan Donnelly. The film is directed by Ellyn Stern.
The Welsh language version was announced at the National Eisteddfod in Pembrokeshire in August
The Welsh-language version was announced at the National Eisteddfod in Pembrokeshire in August, with Lucasfilm co-president Lynwen Brennan saying the franchise was keen to expand its horizons.
"As someone who was born and raised in Wales, seeing the audience reaction to iconic Star Wars moments retold in the Welsh language was a moment of great pride," she said.
S4C chief executive Geraint Evans added that working with "one of the most iconic and influential film franchises of all time is a tremendous honour".
"It is a unique opportunity to introduce the Welsh language to new audiences around the world, while showcasing Wales and its exceptional creative talent on a global stage," he said.

Actors Mark Lewis Jones and Osian Morgan, who voiced characters in dub of 1977 film, among guests on red carpet
It has been a memorable few days for Wales. At the weekend, the men’s rugby team secured a historic win against New Zealand – their first victory over the All Blacks in more than 70 years. Then on Thursday evening came another culturally significant moment when Cardiff rolled out the red carpet to celebrate the first Welsh-language dub of the Star Wars franchise.
Stars of stage and screen who voiced the words of Luke Skywalker, Darth Vader, C-3PO et al in Welsh (Cymraeg) over the original 1977 Star Wars film took the plaudits at the Cineworld Cardiff screening.
Among those on the red carpet was Mark Lewis Jones, who has appeared in shows ranging from The Crown to Game of Thrones and had a role in the 2017 Star Wars film The Last Jedi. In this version of Star Wars, he is a Welsh Darth Vader.
He said he thought Welsh was a good language for Vader. “It has an ancient, poetic sense. It gives him that status, that authority,” said Jones, who hails from the Wrexham area in north-east Wales . “I give all my characters north-east Wales accents,” he said.
Also taking a bow was Osian Morgan – well known in Wales for his appearances in the Welsh-language soap opera Pobol y Cwm – who voices Luke Skywalker.
“There’s so much excitement about this project and the cast is unbelievable,” Morgan said. “I think in Wales we’re on an upward trajectory and this instils a lot of hope. The future is exciting for Wales, particularly in the creative arts. The talent is vast.”
Asked if he felt the pressure of being Luke Skywalker, he said he was thrilled rather than nervous. “He’s had such an important impact on my life,” he said. Morgan was also pleased that his 10-year-old brother’s first experience of Star Wars would be in the medium of Welsh. “The fact that Luke tonight in the Welsh language can have that impact on kids here is fantastic.”
Rhys Ifans, who has appeared in Harry Potter and Spider-Man films, had the tough job of standing in for Alec Guinness as the Jedi master Obi-Wan Kenobi. Sadly, he did not make it to Cardiff for the event.
His brother, Llŷr Ifans, the Welsh voice of the droid C-3PO, was present, however, which was apposite as C-3PO is “fluent in over 6 million forms of communication” – including, clearly, Welsh.
Ifans said: “When I first heard about it, I thought: wow, what are we doing – Star Wars in Welsh? The idea has settled. C-3PO is a genius who speaks over 6 million languages. Now he speaks 6 million and one. He speaks the best language in the world.”
Asked what accent he used for his C-3PO, Ifans said: “There are no accents in space. But it’s more about the character. He lives on his nerves and speaks staccato. I had to bring in those aspects.”
The Welsh-language version of the 1977 film (subsequently retitled Star Wars: Episode IV – A New Hope) has been produced by Lucasfilm and Disney in collaboration with the Welsh-language broadcaster S4C and the Welsh government via its Creative Wales agency.
Its Welsh title is Star Wars: Gobaith Newydd (New Hope). Those not lucky enough to be at the screening in Cardiff will be able to hear the immortal line “May the Force be with you” in Welsh (“A boed i’r Grym fod gyda chi”) when the version is broadcast on S4C platforms on Christmas Day.
Thursday’s screening wasn’t as glitzy as a London or Los Angeles premiere, but it had charm. Côr Bechgyn Glantaf, a schoolboys’ choir from Cardiff, performed as the crowds – including many children – arrived and made their way up the escalators of the multiplex to screens eight and nine. Band Pres Llareggub, which bills itself as a Bronx hip-hop-inspired, New Orleans-tinged brass band with attitude from north Wales, also provided a musical backdrop.
S4C’s chief executive, Geraint Evans, described the screening as a “hugely proud moment”. He said: “Most importantly, it will give Welsh-speaking children the thrill of hearing some of cinema’s most beloved characters speak their language for the very first time, showing that Welsh can tell any story.”
There are a few connections linking Wales and Star Wars, not least that a version of the Millennium Falcon was built in south-west Wales .
Mark Williams, who oversaw an exhibition about the Millennium Falcon, said he felt the Welsh-language version of the film was long overdue. “I’ve been saying for years it should be done, especially with the ties that Wales has with the franchise,” he said.
Also at the screening was the cabinet minister for enterprise, connectivity and energy in the Welsh government, Adam Price, who said it was an excellent opportunity for Welsh actors and production staff to work with a major Hollywood studio.
“Seeing one of the most iconic films of all time in Welsh is a great way to make the language more accessible and introduces it to new audiences beyond our shores,” he said.
The Welsh government is aiming to have a million people speaking Cymraeg by 2050. A spokesperson for the Welsh language commissioner’s office said one of its key aims was to increase the use of the language on a community level.
The spokesperson said: “In order to do this, the language must be seen and heard in all aspects of our daily lives. The use of Welsh in such a high-profile film as Star Wars has the potential to attract new audiences and raise awareness of the language.”

Vodafone Sultanlar Ligi ekibi Aras Kargo'da sporcular ve teknik ekip üyeleri gıda zehirlenmesi şüphesiyle tedavi altına alındı. Bazı voleybolcular hastanede tedavi görürken kulüp, cumartesi günü oynanacak Fenerbahçe Medicana maçının ertelenmesi için Türkiye Voleybol Federasyonu'na resmî başvuruda bulundu. Rahatsızlıklar Eczacıbaşı Peron İstanbul deplasmanı öncesinde başlamıştı.
Kulübün sosyal medya hesabından yaptığı 'Kamuoyuna Duyuru' başlıklı açıklamaya göre belirtiler, Eczacıbaşı Peron İstanbul ile oynanan deplasman karşılaşmasından önce ortaya çıktı. Hem sporcularda hem de teknik ekip üyelerinde gıda zehirlenmesi şüphesi yaratan şikâyetler görüldü.
Maçın ardından sporcuların ve teknik ekibin tedavisine başlandı. Aralarından bazı isimler hastanede tedavi altına alındı. Kulüp, sağlık durumlarının yakından takip edildiğini belirtti, geçmiş olsun dileklerini iletti ve gelişmelerin kamuoyuyla paylaşılacağını duyurdu.
Aras Kargo, Kadınlar Kupa Voley çeyrek finalinde Eczacıbaşı Peron İstanbul 'un konuğuydu. Kulübün açıklamasına göre rahatsızlık maça başlamadan hissedilmişti ve oyun ilerledikçe ağırlaştı. Buna rağmen voleybolcular sahada kaldı, kulüp bunu 'sorumluluk bilinciyle' müsabakayı tamamlamak diye anlattı.
Aynı şikâyetler teknik ekipte de vardı. Yani yalnızca oyuncular değil, kenardan maçı yöneten isimler de kötü hissederek karşılaşmayı sürdürdü.
Karşılaşma 3-0 Eczacıbaşı Peron İstanbul lehine sonuçlandı. Vodafone Sultanlar Ligi'nin İzmir temsilcisi Aras Kargo'nun açıklamasında ise skordan çok sporcuların sağlığı öne çıktı.
Müsabakanın bitmesinin ardından sporcular ve teknik ekip için tedavi süreci başlatıldı, bazı voleybolcular hastanede tedavi altına alındı. Kulüp, kupa maçının sonucuna dair bir değerlendirme yapmak yerine yaşanan sağlık sorunlarına dikkat çekti.
Vodafone Sultanlar Ligi'nin 10. haftasında Aras Kargo, 21 Kasım Cumartesi günü saat 15.00'te İzmir 'de Fenerbahçe Medicana'yı konuk edecek. Kulüp, yaşanan sağlık sorunları gerekçesiyle bu karşılaşmanın ertelenmesi için Türkiye Voleybol Federasyonu'na resmî başvuruda bulundu.
Başvuruyla ilgili kararı federasyon verecek. Sporcuların tedavisi sürerken maçın cumartesi günü oynanıp oynanmayacağı henüz belli değil. Federasyonun kararının kısa süre içinde açıklanması bekleniyor.

Haitian security forces launched a major offensive on Thursday to retake Martissant, a strategic corridor linking Port-au-Prince with the country's western and southern regions that gangs have controlled for five years. Police said at least 34 suspected gang members were killed in clashes involving a private security task force.
Armed forces in Haiti launched an aggressive operation on Thursday to remove powerful gangs long entrenched in a key corridor that connects the country’s capital to its western and southern regions.
It is the first significant operation in the five years since violent gangs seized control of Martissant, located in the western tip of Port-au-Prince.
Haiti’s National Police posted a video on X stating that at least 34 suspected gang members were killed in Martissant during a fight with police officers working with a task force composed of members from Vectus Global, a private security firm founded by former US Navy SEAL and Blackwater founder Erik Prince.
Local media reported heavy gunfire and explosive drones in the area as Haiti’s police posted a video of armoured vehicles rumbling through the community.
To display this content from YouTube, you must enable advertisement tracking and audience measurement.
One of your browser extensions seems to be blocking the video player from loading. To watch this content, you may need to disable it on this site.
Martissant is located along Route 2, the main road that leads out of Port-au-Prince to important western and southern cities. Thousands of people would travel through Martissant every day before gangs seized control of the area more than five years ago, disrupting the country’s economy as they prevented goods from entering or leaving the capital. Gangs have since charged tolls or randomly opened fire on cars or buses that dare cross through.
Ever since gangs seized absolute control of Martissant, aid workers and Haitian civilians have been forced to take alternative transportation or use rural back roads.
The fight to control Martissant began in June 2021, when gangs from Grand-Ravine and Village-de-Dieu attacked the Ti-Bois gang. Armed men set fire to homes, killed families, destroyed businesses and seized control of Martissant’s police station.
The clashes forced at least 19,000 people to flee their homes and affected some 800,000 people overall, according to a July 2022 United Nations report.
Several years ago, gangs operating between Tabarre and Carrefour would demand some $380 from those transiting through Martissant, according to a 2023 UN report.
Read more Haitians rally behind Bukele as Salvadoran troops battle gangs
Last year, Haiti ’s Center for Analysis and Research in Human Rights noted that ever since Martissant fell, hundreds of public and private institutions were relocated and more than one million people were forced to flee their homes.
As the fight in Martissant continues, a UN-backed gang suppression force also has made recent inroads against gangs in a push to not only displace them but prevent their return.
“Operations are entering a new phase: increasing pressure on gang networks, dismantling more strongholds, and extending control over strategic areas,” the force wrote Thursday on X.
The gang suppression force said it’s working in places including Tabarre in Port-au-Prince and in Haiti’s central Artibonite region, which has come under repeated violent attacks by armed men.
The force said it has come under fire as it advances along Route 5, “removing obstacles established by gangs to isolate communities and control key routes.”
Read more Haitian police retake national stadium after two years of gang control
The force said it also cleared and secured a church and school that gangs had been controlling north of Gros-Morne.
“It is about restoring freedom of movement, reopening access to public institutions, and re-establishing State presence for communities that have endured years of gang control,” the force wrote Sunday on X.
Also fighting gangs are some 2,500 troops deployed by El Salvador last month when four of their own went missing after an October 18 attack in Haiti’s capital.
Following orders by Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele , the troops have attacked the main homes of two of Haiti’s most powerful gang leaders, Jeff and Lanmò San Jou, this month. Neither one was killed.
Read more Amnesty urges El Salvador to disclose terms of Haiti troop deployment
Thousands of Haitians poured into the streets of Port-au-Prince and beyond this week in support of Bukele, but experts have criticised the unilateral operations of Salvadoran troops and noted that the use of explosive drones has claimed a growing number of innocent victims.
A small group of Salvadorans are separately working with the gang suppression force.
In late September, El Salvador’s legislature passed a law authorising the participation of that group in Haiti for another 12 months until October 2027. The law was championed by Bukele and overwhelmingly approved by the country’s congress, controlled by Bukele’s party.
The ongoing clashes with gangs continue as Haiti prepares for its first elections in more than a decade. The country hasn't had a president since Jovenel Moïse was killed in July 2021.

Anthropic 18 Kasım'da halka arz kapsamında hisse başına 83 dolardan 980 milyon adet hisseyi satışa sundu.
Böylece halka arzın temel büyüklüğü 81,3 milyar dolar olarak hesaplanırken Anthropic, SpaceX'i geride bırakarak tüm zamanların en büyük halka arzına imza attı.
Bu rekor, yapay zeka ve ileri teknoloji şirketlerinin halka arz hacimlerini önceki dönemlere kıyasla katladığını gösterdi. Uzun yıllar boyunca 20 ila 25 milyar dolar bandında seyreden küresel rekorlar, bu yıl önce SpaceX, ardından Anthropic ile 3-4 katına ulaştı.
Nasdaq borsasında işlem görmeye başlayan Anthropic'in hisseleri, 111,5 dolardan yüzde 34,3 primle açılış yaptı.
Anthropic ayrıca, aracı kurumlara 147 milyon adede kadar ek hisse senedi satın alma konusunda 30 günlük opsiyon tanıdı.
Tarihin en büyük halka arzları listesinde ilk iki sırayı ABD merkezli teknoloji ve yapay zeka devlerinin alması dikkati çekti.
Renaissance Capital'ın verilerine göre, aracı kurumlara tanınan ek satış opsiyonları hariç tutulduğunda, toplanan fon büyüklüğü açısından küresel borsalarda bugüne kadar gerçekleştirilen en büyük 10 halka arz Anthropic, SpaceX, SK hynix, Saudi Aramco, Alibaba, SoftBank, NTT Mobile, Visa, AIA ve ENEL SpA olarak sıralandı.
Söz konusu sıralamada, Çin Tarım Bankası (AgBank) ve Çin Endüstri ve Ticaret Bankasının (ICBC) Şanghay ile Hong Kong borsalarındaki eş zamanlı halka arzları ayrı ayrı hesaplandığı için bu işlemler ilk 10'da yer almadı.

Güçlü yorumuyla yıllardır kalplere dokunmayı başaran Yonca Lodi , yeni şarkısında masum bir sevgi arayışını, bu arayışta yaşanan hayal kırıklıklarını ve içsel bir sitemi merkeze alıyor. “Yaprak Dökümü Leyla”, etrafındaki sahte mutluluklar ve yüzeysel ilişkiler arasında, sadece gerçek ve sade bir bağ kurmak isteyen kırgın bir kalbin duygu yüklü isyanını anlatıyor. Dinleyiciler, şarkının dokunaklı atmosferinde kendi yalnızlıklarından ve hayata karşı sitemlerinden tanıdık izler bulacak.
Dikkat çeken şarkının arkasında müzik sektörünün tecrübeli ve başarılı isimleri yer alıyor. Eserin söz ve müziği, son dönemde hit şarkılara imza atan Murat Güneş’e ait. Şarkının duygusal yoğunluğunu modern ve etkileyici bir altyapıyla buluşturan düzenleme ise usta aranjör Mehmethan Dişbudak’ın imzasını taşıyor. Şarkının ruhunu görsel dünyayla bütünleştiren ve hikâyenin melankolik yapısını ekrana taşıyan video klibin yönetmen koltuğunda ise Emrah Özbilen oturuyor.
20 Kasım 2026 itibarıyla müzik dünyasına giriş yapacak olan “Yaprak Dökümü Leyla”, aynı gün video klibiyle de dijital platformlarda ve müzik kanallarında izleyiciyle buluşacak.
90’ların efsanevi Bristol Sound atmosferinden ilham alan “Yağmur”, Teoman’ın güçlü vokali ve genç sanatçı Yağmur Erdağ’ın kırılgan sesiyle dinleyiciyle buluşuyor. Bazen bir şarkı sizi aşka değil, ayrılığa davet eder. Bazen de ilk notalarından itibaren sizi bambaşka bir müzikal dünyanın içine çeker. Teoman ve genç sanatçı Yağmur Erdağ’ı bir araya getiren “Yağmur”, tam da böyle bir şarkı.
Ayrılık, yalnızlık ve umutsuzluğun izlerini taşıyan bu özel buluşmada, Yağmur Erdağ’ın naif, kırılgan ve hüzünlü vokali, Teoman ’ın karakteristik ve güçlü sesiyle buluşuyor. Ancak “Yağmur’u farklı kılan yalnızca bu iki sesin birlikteliği değil. Şarkı, alışılmış müzik kalıplarının dışına çıkan atmosferi ve farklı ses tasarımıyla da dikkat çekiyor. Bristol Sound’un karanlık atmosferi, günümüzün müzikal diliyle yeniden hayat buluyor. 90’lı yılların İngiliz müzik sahnesinde kendine özgü bir yer edinen Bristol Sound akımını hatırlayanlar için “Yağmur”un dünyası oldukça tanıdık, ancak bir o kadar da yeni. Massive Attack ve Portishead’in öncülük ettiği, Morcheeba ve Goldfrapp gibi isimlerin farklı yorumlarla zenginleştirdiği atmosferik müzik anlayışından izler taşıyan şarkı, bu mirası günümüzün prodüksiyon yaklaşımıyla yeniden yorumluyor.
Hip-hop ritimleri, dub ve reggae etkili bas yürüyüşleri, melodik rock gitarları ve karanlık elektronik dokular… Birbirinden farklı müzikal unsurların buluştuğu “Yağmur”, dinleyicisini daha ilk dinleyişte içine çeken sinematografik bir atmosfer yaratıyor.
Ankara’lı müzisyen Timur Tikriti’nin söz ve bestesine imza attığı şarkının aranjman ve kayıtları Taylan Erdağ ve Timur Tikriti tarafından gerçekleştirildi. Ses tasarımı, kayıt ve final mix aşamasında Tolga Görsev’in de yer aldığı prodüksiyon, farklı müzikal katmanları ve kendine özgü ses tasarımıyla da öne çıkıyor.
DANS BİTTİ, DERT BAŞLADI: TEKİR’DEN “BOOMBESK” Yaz boyunca roman ritimleriyle dinleyicilerini dans ettiren Tekir, yeni albümü “BoomBesk” ile bu kez kalplere dokunmaya geliyor.
Arabeskin derin hüznünü boom bap ritimleriyle buluşturan sanatçı, sekiz şarkıdan oluşan albümünde dinleyicilerini aşkın, özlemin ve kalp kırıklıklarının izinde duygusal bir yolculuğa çıkarıyor… Dinleyicilerinin uzun zamandır beklediği o dertli Tekir , “BoomBesk” ile müzikal yolculuğunun farklı bir yüzünü ortaya koyuyor. Hareketli ritimlerin yerini içten hikâyelere, dansın yerini geçmişi hatırlatan duygulara bıraktığı albümde sanatçı, arabeskin zamansız ruhunu günümüzün sound’uyla bir araya getiriyor. Tamamı yeni ve özgün şarkılardan oluşan proje, Tekir’in kendine has yorumuyla dinleyicinin kalbine dokunmayı hedefliyor. Albümün odak şarkısı “Susma N’olur”, “BoomBesk”in duygusal atmosferini temsil ederken projenin merkezindeki aşkı, kırgınlığı ve özlemi ön plana çıkarıyor. Sekiz şarkının tamamında söz ve müziğe imza atan Tekir, kendi hikâyelerini kendi kelimeleriyle anlatıyor. Albümde “Yağsın”, “Susma N’olur”, “Düştüm Zorlara”, “Beni Yordu Bu Kavga”, “Tutunduğum Dala Kırgınım”, “Gayrı Sevme”, “Yol Alır Herkes” ve “Uğrarım Bir Ara” isimli sekiz şarkı yer alıyor. Albümün düzenlemeleri TKR, mix ve mastering çalışmaları ise Buğra Kunt imzası taşıyor.

Kurtaran, Yaprak Dökümü'nün yanı sıra Eşkıya Dünyaya Hükümdar Olmaz, Aşk ve Ceza, Huzur Sokağı, Bir Deniz Hikayesi, Tek Yürek ve Hudutsuz Sevda gibi dizilerde yer aldı. Brydon stars in a new series Bill's Included as well-intentioned but overly enthusiastic divorcé Bill Beam
Rob Brydon has revealed he pretended to be his own agent at the start of his career when he was working as a TV and radio presenter in Wales.
The actor, best known for playing Stacey's Uncle Bryn in the hit sitcom Gavin and Stacey, told BBC One's Graham Norton Show , external he used to step into the role of his fake agent to arrange bookings for events.
"I would get asked to go and do things, and I didn't really have an agent at that time so I invented a guy called Richard Knight," Brydon told the show.
The fictional agent would phone organisers and negotiate a fee for Brydon's appearance, he said.
The actor, who grew up in Baglan, Port Talbot, shared an anecdote about being invited to a fundraiser and managing to get a fee for it.
"I'm terribly embarrassed," he told the show's host and fellow guests Cynthia Erivo, David Tennant and Laura Linney.
"They were all there for the good of their hearts," he said.
Brydon, known for his ability to mimic a range of celebrities, went on to impersonate the fictional Richard Knight asking for money in return for an appearance, with the agent describing Brydon as "an angel".
"I would go to these events and they would say 'oh I spoke to Mr Knight, he's quite a character', and I would say 'more than you realise'," Brydon told the show.
The 61-year-old actor stars in new sitcom Bill's Included in which he plays Bill Beam, a divorced man who rents his spare rooms to four students to stay financially afloat while "trying his very best to be their friend".
He told the Press Association he was drawn to his latest comedy role because he had missed acting in sitcoms since featuring in Gavin and Stacey.
The popular show ended in January 2010, although Christmas specials aired in 2019 and 2024.
While Brydon has since hosted shows including Destination X and Would I Lie To You?, the new show marks his return to the sitcom format.
"He calls himself a land-friend, not a landlord," Brydon said of his character Bill Beam.
Bill's Included will follow Bill and his lodgers as they muddle through "chaos, growing pains and unexpected friendships"
Dylan Brady, Ada Player, Harry Baxendale and Yasmin Al-Khudhairi join the cast as Bill's student lodgers Christian, Hettie, James and Zahra.
Brydon praised the young actors, saying he "loved being around them, partly because of their energy".
He said he also enjoyed hearing their perspective on the industry.
"They knew who was being cast in what, who was directing which projects and it reminded me of how I used to be," he said.
The actor also remarked on the "odd" feeling of being told by some of the actors that they grew up watching him on television.
He said: "I remember that at the end of filming, one of them said to me, 'Thanks for being nice and for spending time with us between set-ups'.
"My reaction was, 'Well, of course I did. We're all actors on this show.'"
Bill's Included will be available on BBC iPlayer and BBC One from 20 November.

Yıllardır beklenen Grand Theft Auto VI, 19 Kasım’da PlayStation 5 ve Xbox Series X|S için çıktı. Biz de oyunun çıkışıyla birlikte şu sorunun peşine düştük. Her hafta izlediğimiz Türk dizileri GTA evrenine taşınsaydı afişleri nasıl görünürdü? Yeraltı’ndan Tuzlu Kahve ’ye sekiz dizinin orijinal afişini Vice City esintili yorumlarıyla yan yana getirdik.
Orijinal afişte yer alan arka plandaki apartmanların yerini gün batımına karşı uzanan gökdelenler alıyor. Ön tarafta mor bir otomobil , gökyüzünde ise bir helikopter var. Bu afiş oyunun açılış ekranında karşımıza çıksa, ilk görevin kimin tarafından verileceğini tahmin etmek çok da zor olmazdı.
Uzak Şehir ’in orijinal afişindeki taş konak, yeni yorumun da merkezinde. Bu kez taş avluya pembe ve turuncu bir gün batımı vuruyor, kadrajı da palmiyeler çevreliyor. Oyunun haritasında böyle bir konak görsek, içeride anlatılacakları merak edip ana görevi biraz erteleyebilirdik.
Orijinal afişteki perdeler ve kırmızı halı, GTA esintili yorumda yerini palmiyelere ve sahil manzarasına bırakıyor. Smokinler, gece elbiseleri ve o ciddi aile pozu ise olduğu gibi duruyor. Bu haliyle afişe bakınca insanın aklına tek bir soru geliyor. Vice City’de bir aile davetine katılmak, başlı başına bir görev sayılır mı?
Orijinal afişin geniş, gri gökyüzü bu kez pembe, mor ve turuncuya dönüyor. Karakterlerin arkasında kayalık bir kıyı, ahşap bir ev ve uzakta bir deniz feneri beliriyor. Sekiz afiş arasında en belirgin manzara değişimlerinden biri burada. Şehir merkezinden çıkıp kıyı yolunu takip etsek, bu kadronun karşımıza çıkacağı yer tam da burası olurdu.
Teşkilat ’ın altıncı sezon afişinde sırt sırta duran ikili, GTA esintili versiyonda da pozunu koruyor. Gri duvarların yerini suyun karşısındaki gökdelenler, helikopter ve gün batımı alıyor. Ön plana eklenen otomobille birlikte kare, görev başlamadan hemen önce ekrana gelen bir tanıtım görselini andırıyor.
Orijinal afişin aksine bu kez ikilinin arkasında gün batımına karşı yükselen gökdelenler ve suyun üzerinde bir yat var. Afişi ilk bakışta tanımamızı sağlayan ayrıntı yine o gül.
Orijinaldeki dağ manzarası, GTA esintili versiyonda gün batımının renklerine bürünüyor. Kadrajın üst köşelerine eklenen palmiyeler de oyunun havasını taşıyor. Ortaya, haritanın dağlık tarafında durup çekilmiş bir düğün selfiesi çıkmış.
Orijinal afişte sarı bir zemin üzerinde koltuklara dağılan kalabalık kadro, yeni yorumda gün batımına karşı oturuyor. Fincanlar ve abajur yerinde, arkada ise palmiyeler, su ve gökdelenler var.

Late-night hosts discussed Trump’s friendly meeting with the Russian and Chinese leaders at the Apec summit
Late-night hosts mocked Donald Trump ’s friendly meeting with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping as well as the administration’s muddled response to various tech outages.
Jimmy Kimmel opened Wednesday’s show with footage of Trump’s visit to the Apec summit in Shenzhen, China, where the president “got a rare personal greeting on the tarmac from President Xi”.
Kimmel then played footage of Trump disembarking Air Force One to receive a warm embrace from the Chinese leader. “You know, President Xi doesn’t usually do that sort of thing, but I guess he wanted to see what a $400m bribe from Qatar looks like up close,” the host joked, referring to Trump’s new Air Force One aircraft, a $400m “gift” from Qatar.
“Trump was excited to be reunited with his friend, the Chinese president,” he added. “You know, it’s been a while. He finally has new male buttocks to fixate on.
“Funny, Trump spent the last 10 years calling Democrats communists,” he quipped. “He gets off the plane, gives a big wet kiss to an actual communist, a real one.
“But he put his best hoof forward,” Kimmel continued, noting that the president “painted his hands real pretty for the event” with obvious putty-like makeup that did not match his skin tone.
“This hand has now been paved over more times than his name at the Kennedy Center,” Kimmel joked. “Either that’s his makeup or he’s eating peanut butter straight out of the jar again.”
Kimmel then played footage of Trump and Xi joined on the red carpet by the Russian leader, Vladimir Putin, whom the US president once again referred to as his “friend” .
“I guess Darth Vader couldn’t make it to fill out the foursome,” Kimmel wisecracked. “There you see Trump reunited with the leader of the country that makes his merch, and the leader of the country that made him president.
“You can tell Trump feels jealous when he meets with Xi and Putin and sees all the cool dictator stuff they get to do,” he added. “It’s like when you’re a kid and you visit your cousin who had Sega Genesis.”
And on Late Night, Seth Meyers reacted to the recent cascade of tech outages. “I don’t know if you guys have noticed this lately, but it feels like things are breaking. And by things, I mean all the things,” he said before listing technical failures at Microsoft , major US banks , Apple , American air traffic control systems and the National Security Agency all in the last week. The causes have been vague; JP Morgan Chase, for one, attributed their outage to “technical issues”.
“Oh, is it a ‘technical issue’?” Meyers deadpanned. “The problems we’re having with the internet and routers and AI aren’t caused by Mercury in retrograde or someone made a badly worded wish on the novelty toy from Obsession.”
But not to fret – the homeland security secretary, Markwayne Mullin, was on the case, appearing this week on Fox News to reassure the public that “the homeland is secure. Our banking system is secure. And when something like this happens, we’re able to react, and react fast. You see what happened Friday night with the FAA.”
“Yeah, we did. That sucked!” Meyers responded. “The nation’s air traffic control system broke down because of a router somewhere in Arkansas?”
In the same interview, Mullin tried to reassure viewers that he spoke to one anonymous “guy that’s very smart with tech”, who explained that AI – or “SI”, to use the preferred parlance of the Trump administration – “self-fixes itself. As it starts self-fixing itself, it’s like doing a change order on house. When you do a change order on a house, everything else starts changing and it’s a ripple effect.” That long explanation “kinda made sense to me”, he added.
“Does it? Because it makes no fucking sense to me,” Meyers said. “You sound like a gym teacher subbing in for health class – ‘OK team, listen up, when the egg comes down and self-fixes itself with the sperm, think of it like a running back carrying the ball through the gap, and you know there’s a ripple effect.’”
